name: Normalize audio loudness to broadcast/social standards with FFmpeg

parameters.content:
## Normalize any audio file to broadcast loudness with FFmpeg (free, no API)

Upload an audio file, pick a target loudness, and get back a normalized file plus the exact loudness numbers FFmpeg measured - before and after. No API key, no account, no paid service: everything runs on FFmpeg's own `loudnorm` filter, the same EBU R128 loudness algorithm broadcasters use, called for free on your own machine.

This is the loudness-normalization step from a larger faceless-video pipeline, pulled out on its own because it is useful far beyond video - podcasters, video editors, and anyone shipping a voiceover that sounds noticeably quieter or louder than everything else in a feed needs this exact step.

**Customization built in:** an optional low-cut (highpass) filter runs before normalization, so a rough recording's room rumble, AC hum, or handling noise gets stripped in the same pass instead of being normalized along with the voice.

### How it works

1. A form takes an audio file, a target loudness (YouTube/TikTok/Spotify at -14 LUFS, podcast platforms at -16, EBU broadcast at -23, or a quieter -19), and an optional low-cut frequency.
2. The file is saved to a per-run temp folder so concurrent submissions never collide.
3. If a low-cut was chosen, FFmpeg's `highpass` filter removes everything below that frequency first; then the `loudnorm` filter measures the (now-cleaned) input's loudness and true peak and normalizes it to your target in one pass, printing both the measured input and the achieved output as JSON.
4. That JSON is parsed into a clean report: input LUFS, output LUFS, true peak, target, and whether a low-cut was applied.
5. The normalized audio file is read back off disk and returned alongside the report.

### Setup

Self-hosted n8n only - this uses Execute Command, which n8n Cloud disables. Install FFmpeg on the PATH of the process running n8n, and start n8n with `NODES_EXCLUDE="[]"` and `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO="/tmp"` - both are required or the file steps fail without a clear error.

## 1. Upload
Any format FFmpeg reads: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg. Optional low-cut (highpass) filter to strip rumble/hum first.

## 2. Save to disk
Written to a per-run temp folder so concurrent runs never collide.

## 3. Measure + normalize
One FFmpeg pass measures input loudness and normalizes to your target, printing both as JSON.

## 4. Report + deliver
Parses the real measured numbers and returns them next to the normalized file.

## Self-hosted only
Execute Command does not exist on n8n Cloud. See Setup in the overview.

nodes.name: Audio file and target loudness form
nodes.notes: Entry point. Downstream nodes read the uploaded file's binary and the Target Loudness dropdown from here.

parameters.formDescription: Upload an audio file, pick a target loudness, and optionally a low-cut frequency to strip rumble/hum first. You get back a normalized file plus the real loudness numbers FFmpeg measured, before and after.

nodes.name: Prepare Run
nodes.notes: Builds a per-run temp folder, detects the uploaded file's binary property name (doesn't assume it), and parses the numeric LUFS target out of the dropdown label.

nodes.name: Create the temp folder
nodes.notes: mkdir -p is safe to run again. This wipes json + binary, restored in the next node.

nodes.name: Restore the uploaded file
nodes.notes: Execute Command replaces the item with its own stdout/stderr/exitCode - re-attach the uploaded file's binary and the paths from Prepare Run.

nodes.name: Save the uploaded file to disk
nodes.notes: Writes the uploaded audio to the temp folder so FFmpeg (Execute Command) can read it by path.

nodes.name: Measure and normalize loudness (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: loudnorm measures the input then normalizes to the target in one pass, printing a JSON stats block (input/output LUFS + true peak) to stderr - that block is the real measurement, parsed in the next node. Reads paths from Prepare Run, not $json, since this node's own output replaces both.

nodes.name: Parse the loudness report
nodes.notes: Extracts and parses FFmpeg's loudnorm JSON stats block from stderr. Throws with the real FFmpeg error if the exit code was not 0, instead of silently returning a broken file path.

nodes.name: Read the normalized audio back
nodes.notes: Reads the normalized file off disk as binary output - the free-path deliverable, no external service involved.

nodes.name: Attach the loudness report to the file
nodes.notes: Read/Write File's read operation replaces json with file metadata only - merges the loudness report back in so the output has both the numbers and the file.

main.node: Save the uploaded file to disk
Attach the loudness report to the file
